### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via getMetaItem (symbol, a method of interface McpMergedMetadataRead))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via getMetaItem (symbol, a method of interface McpMergedMetadataRead))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via getMetaItem (symbol, a method of interface McpMergedMetadataRead))_
- `content/docs/frontend/data-objectstack.mdx`  _(via /app/:appId/bundle (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItem — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via getPublished (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getPublished, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/published; the bare tail of client method meta.getPublished, bound to GET /meta/:type/:name/published))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via getMetaItem (symbol, a method of interface McpMergedMetadataRead))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx`  _(via /object/:name/state/:field (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItem — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via getLegalNextStates (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getLegalNextStates, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name/state/:field; the bare tail of client method meta.getLegalNextStates, bound to GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field), meta.getLegalNextStates (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name/state/:field, selected by route anchor /object/:name/state/:field; the route ledger binds it to GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field, selected by route anchor /object/:name/state/:field))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-2.mdx`  _(via getLegalNextStates (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getLegalNextStates, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name/state/:field; the bare tail of client method meta.getLegalNextStates, bound to GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field), meta.getLegalNextStates (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name/state/:field, selected by route anchor /object/:name/state/:field; the route ledger binds it to GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field, selected by route anchor /object/:name/state/:field))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via /:type/:name/published (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItem — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via /app/:appId/bundle (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItem — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 158cc2aa53449b903939f936bad466d8cd0e2e2b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d512ae5b3cdca9c45251b7205df0dfb05b229f97` — the merge of head `863aa0f5ca94e3d9b352d76e1b7e5ff81c4803e0` into base `158cc2aa53449b903939f936bad466d8cd0e2e2b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d512ae5b3cdca9c45251b7205df0dfb05b229f97 && git checkout d512ae5b3cdca9c45251b7205df0dfb05b229f97
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 158cc2aa53449b903939f936bad466d8cd0e2e2b 863aa0f5ca94e3d9b352d76e1b7e5ff81c4803e0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 158cc2aa53449b903939f936bad466d8cd0e2e2b && git merge --no-ff 863aa0f5ca94e3d9b352d76e1b7e5ff81c4803e0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 158cc2aa53449b903939f936bad466d8cd0e2e2b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 158cc2aa53449b903939f936bad466d8cd0e2e2b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `959a0c6160e6f45c1a72c4dbe44f07da9807de97`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #31514 (body, triage 1, seat 5's re-read lifting `Blocked-by: #30806`, the seat 6 claim, the os-dev-report), PR #31565 (body, the 4-file list, the net diff against `origin/main` `2c6b9364`), and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read at the head and not reviewed.

- **The by-name read is the one `GET /api/v1/meta/agent/NAME` serves. RIGHT.** The uncached arm of `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts` calls `p.getMetaItem({ type, name, packageId })`, and the cached arm calls `getMetaItemCached`, which delegates to `getMetaItem`. With no `?package=`, `packageId` is undefined, which is the request `readAgentByName` sends. After the read the door runs `createMetaItemAnswer`: a per-caller read gate (it has no `agent` arm), the mask, and `translateMetaDocument`. `agent` is not in `METADATA_DOCUMENT_TRANSLATORS` (`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`). So for an agent, `item` holds the same document the REST body carries. Both protocol mounts (`MetadataProtocolPlugin` and ObjectQLPlugin's `registerProtocol`) register the same `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` through `assembleMetadataProtocol`. The spec's `MetadataProtocol` declares `getMetaItem` as required. The dogfood twin compares the served text with the kernel's own `protocol.getMetaItem`, on all four boot rows.
- **The protocol read brings in the protocol's own withholding. RIGHT, as REST parity.** `getMetaItem` answers ABSENT for a non-`package` item of a disabled package, so `agent_prompt` now answers `not found` there, as the REST door and the listing do. Its overlay step throws `metadataStoreUnavailableError` (`code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE'`, 503) when `sys_metadata` cannot be read. A code-shipped agent that the metadata service used to serve during that outage now gets the outage text. That is what `/meta/agent/NAME` answers in the same outage. The one-reader ruling wants this, but the changeset does not name it (see the nit in ③).
- **`readAgentByName`: one reader on the get side, with no merging fallback. RIGHT.** When `getMetaItem` is present, only the protocol is asked. When it is absent, only `diagnosedGet(metadataService, …)` is asked. No path tries one source and then the other. Unit case 2 pins that the metadata double is never asked for the package agent.
- **#6055 outage versus miss. RIGHT.**
  - A throw coded `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` becomes `degraded: true` with no data. `buildAgentPromptResult` then answers `Error: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE — …`, serves no instructions and logs a warn (unit case 5). The protocol throws this only when the whole chain resolved nothing and the service read was degraded (`protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`, after step 3). Before the change, `diagnosedGet` reported degraded in exactly that case.
  - Any other throw is rethrown to the SDK, as a `getDiagnosed`/`get` throw always was.
  - A miss (`item` absent) answers `Error: Agent "X" not found` byte for byte (unit case 4, and the dogfood miss on all four rows).
  - A hit is served as before (CONTROL, unit case 3).
- **#28940 advertisement. RIGHT for every host in the repo.** `readAgentRoster` now reads `mergedDiagnosedList`: items from `getMetaItems({type:'agent'})`, with the completeness verdict still from `listDiagnosed`. That is the skill listing's composition, and it is a verdict, not a second item source. If the roster read throws, the state is `unknown` and the prompt is advertised with no names. Degraded with no names is also `unknown`. Complete with no names is `none`, and the prompt is not listed. A host with no protocol (`mergedRead` undefined) reads `diagnosedList(metadataService)` as before. The listing applies the same disabled-package predicate as the by-name read, so the names the roster teaches are names the get can serve.
- **Every host that builds the runtime passes a `mergedRead` that carries `getMetaItem`. RIGHT.** The only production constructor and `bridgePrompts` caller is `packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts`. It passes the `protocol` service whenever that service has `getMetaItems`, and that service is the full `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`, which has `getMetaItem`. The HTTP door at `/api/v1/mcp` (`buildMcpBridge`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`) registers no `agent_prompt`. `git grep` at the head finds no other `registerPrompt('agent_prompt'` and no other production `bridgePrompts(` call. No host is left on the old reader.
- **should-fix: a `mergedRead` with `getMetaItems` but no `getMetaItem` gets two readers on one host.**
  - The roster switches to the protocol when `getMetaItems` is present (`mergedDiagnosedList`). The get switches only when `getMetaItem` is present (`readAgentByName`). The published type of `bridgePrompts`' second parameter still admits `{ getMetaItems }` alone, and that is every caller's object before this PR.
  - For such a caller this PR changes the roster to the protocol listing but leaves the get on the metadata service. A package agent is then advertised by name, while `prompts/get` answers `not found` for it. That is the #28940 declared-is-served defect, and the two-readers defect this card closes.
  - The changeset's sentence "a host that passes an object without it is read as before" is false for the roster. The `readAgentByName` doc's "ONE reader per host, never both" is not enforced across the two reads.
  - No host in the repo reaches this today: the spec's `MetadataProtocol` requires `getMetaItem`, and `plugin.ts` passes the full protocol. So the grade is should-fix, not must-fix.
  - Fix: gate the roster's protocol listing on the same predicate as the get (`typeof mergedRead?.getMetaItem === 'function'`, else `diagnosedList`), and pin it with a `{ getMetaItems }`-only double. Or keep the code and correct the changeset sentence.
- **nit: pins.** No unit pin covers a non-`SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` throw from `getMetaItem` travelling as a throw. None covers a `getMetaItems`-only read object, which would have caught the should-fix above. None covers a degraded roster under a protocol double. Everything that is pinned matches the code.
- **The test-harness changes are RIGHT.** The dogfood `boot` parameter is narrowed to `{ artifact(): unknown }`, its only use, and `Booted` gains `rpc`. Neither is a published surface.

Gate verdicts, from the check-runs on this head: every one that ran concluded `success`. That covers Build Core, Test Core and its 8 shards, all four TypeScript Type Check jobs, the ESLint and repo-gate Lint jobs, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards and Check PR Size. The skipped runs are the UI, docs and opt-in jobs, which do not apply to this diff, and the dogfood shards. `Dogfood Regression Gate (N/3)` is skipped on `pull_request` by design (ci.yml, #30461). The `Dogfood Regression Gate` success on this head attests zero expected shards. The real-kernel twin in `packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-stdio-package-object-discovery.test.ts` is measured by the merge-queue build, where that gate is required and a red ejects the entry. It is not measured by this head's check-runs.

### ② Semver level

- **`'@objectstack/mcp': patch` is RIGHT.** The diff publishes from one package, `@objectstack/mcp`. The dogfood change is a test file in a QA package. Under AGENTS.md "Add a changeset", a `none` kind takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening also ships `patch`. Check Changeset is `success`.
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` HOLDS.**
  - `McpMergedMetadataRead` gains an optional `getMetaItem` member. The type is not named in `src/index.ts`, but it is published as the declared type of `MCPServerRuntime.bridgePrompts`' second parameter, and `MCPServerRuntime` is exported. An optional member on an input type is a widening: every object a caller passed before still type-checks.
  - The runtime effect is also a widening of what an MCP client is served: package agents are now listed and served.
  - The two serve-side withholdings (a disabled package's agent, and the overlay-store 503) only bring this door into line with what `/meta/agent/NAME` already refuses. They take nothing away that the spec declares, so no `(narrowing)` arm is owed.
  - The line is identical in the PR body and the changeset.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` HOLDS.** No key, accepted value or metadata type that an author can write changes, and the diff does not touch `packages/spec`.
- `buildAgentPromptResult`'s new optional fourth parameter is module-exported but not published by `index.ts`, so it adds nothing to the surface.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`: `[]`.** Nothing is left unanswered.
- **Deviations (no force push; `pr_create` with no labels and no assignees): ANSWERED.**
  - The seat allowed a force-with-lease restart, and the permission layer refused it. The remote branch had been deleted when #31464 merged, so a plain push recreated it from `origin/main`. Nothing was rewritten. The net diff is the 4 claimed files, and the merge of `origin/main` (`6ed533f6`) brings nothing under `packages/mcp` or `packages/qa/dogfood`.
  - No labels and no assignees were set because the order named none. A changeset ships, so no `skip-changeset` is owed.
- **`out_of_scope_findings` (the HTTP `/api/v1/mcp` door has no `agent_prompt`): CONFIRMED.** Only the stdio runtime registers the prompt, so no second surface needed repointing.
- **The card's "Phase 3's namespaced names apply" line is ANSWERED by seat 5's re-read.** That line was replaced by "bare name until #31527 defines the address". The PR reads the bare name, and nothing anticipates #31527.
- **The claim's file surface and prohibitions are HELD.** No `packages/spec/**` change, and no lookup that merges the `metadata` service with the protocol read for one answer. The roster's `listDiagnosed` is a completeness verdict, as for skills. The should-fix in ① is a predicate mismatch between the two reads, not a merging fallback.
- **The provisional `Clause-②` in the claim is ANSWERED.** The dev re-declared it from the diff as `yes (widening)`, and ② above judges that line.
- **The card's pin requirements (red on `main` first, an environment-agent CONTROL) are ANSWERED.** The unit CONTROL is case 3. The red-first and ablation readings are the dev's local measurements, reported in the PR body. This review did not re-run them, by the read-only rule.
- **nit: the PR body misstates CI coverage.** The Verification section says the dogfood battery is carried by "this PR's check-runs". On `pull_request` it is not: the dogfood shards run only on the merge-queue build (see ①).
- **nit: the changeset does not name the protocol's withholding.** A disabled package's agent now answers `not found`, and an overlay-store outage now answers the outage text for a code agent. Both match the REST door, and one changelog sentence would say so.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-mrhms6`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5p3T5YWhLjurajudnQ`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `863aa0f5ca94e3d9b352d76e1b7e5ff81c4803e0`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

This is a delta round on record 6723501040 (head `959a0c61`, PASS with one should-fix). I read card #31514 (body, triage 6721737479, seat 5's re-read 6721960984, the seat 6 claim 6722506414 and the os-dev-report 6723198526). There is no newer dev report. I also read PR #31565 (its body as edited for this head, and the same 4-file list), the net diff against `main` (merge base `6b83ec2d`; `main` at `158cc2aa` adds only #31569, under `packages/service-settings`), the delta `git diff 959a0c61 863aa0f5` and the check-runs on this head. I read code outside the diff but did not review it.

**What moved.** The first-parent commits are `9d09636b` (the fix) and two merges of `origin/main`, `72b76773` and `863aa0f5`. Neither merge changes `packages/mcp` or `packages/qa/dogfood` against its first parent. `git show --remerge-diff` is empty for both, so both are clean automatic merges, with no hand resolution. Under the PR's paths, the delta touches only `.changeset/31514-agent-prompt-protocol-read.md`, `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts` and `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.agent-prompt-advertised.test.ts`. The dogfood twin `packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-stdio-package-object-discovery.test.ts` did not move. The merges also leave untouched everything the earlier record's judgments rest on outside the diff: `packages/rest`, `packages/objectql`, `packages/spec` and `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` (the only non-PR package path in the delta is `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`, which none of those judgments cite). So the earlier judgments on the by-name read and REST parity, the protocol's withholding, #6055 outage versus miss, the production host (`plugin.ts` passes the full `protocol` service) and the dogfood harness are carried unchanged.

- **The earlier should-fix is DISCHARGED.**
  - The new module-private `agentReadOf(mergedRead)` returns `mergedRead` only when both `getMetaItems` and `getMetaItem` are functions. Otherwise it returns `undefined`, which means the metadata service.
  - `bridgePrompts` computes `agentRead = agentReadOf(mergedRead)` once. It passes that value both to `readAgentRoster` (which calls `mergedDiagnosedList(metadataService, agentReadOf(mergedRead), 'agent')`) and to `buildAgentPromptResult` (which calls `readAgentByName`, which calls `agentReadOf` again).
  - So the roster and the get now share one predicate. A `{ getMetaItems }`-only read leaves both on the metadata service. With `undefined`, `mergedDiagnosedList` falls back to `diagnosedList(metadataService, 'agent')`. That is `main`'s read byte for byte, so the corrected changeset sentence "a host that passes an object without it is read as before, the roster included" is now TRUE.
  - The "ONE reader per host" doc on `readAgentByName` is now enforced across both reads, not only stated.
- **Accept-set of the delta, by host shape. RIGHT on every shape.**
  - A read with both members, which includes the only production host, the `protocol` service from `plugin.ts`, behaves as on `959a0c61`: the protocol for both reads.
  - A `{ getMetaItems }`-only read changes from roster-on-protocol plus get-on-metadata to metadata for both. That is the fix, and it is identical to `main`.
  - No read, or a read whose `getMetaItems` is not a function, stays on the metadata service, as before.
  - Skill prompts still take `mergedRead` directly, not `agentReadOf`, so a `{ getMetaItems }`-only host keeps its merged skill listing. The gate is per type, which is right: the skill get never used `getMetaItem`.
- **`buildAgentPromptResult` now runs its `protocol` argument through `agentReadOf`. RIGHT, and no public-surface change.**
  - It is exported from the module but not from `packages/mcp/src/index.ts`, which publishes only `MCPServerRuntime` and the type `MCPServerRuntimeConfig`. The package's `exports` map has only `.`, so the function is not reachable from outside the package.
  - Its fourth parameter is new in this PR, so against `main` nothing published moves. Against `959a0c61`, the only change is that an untyped `{ getMetaItem }`-only argument now reads the metadata service. The parameter's declared type, `McpMergedMetadataRead`, requires `getMetaItems`, so no typed caller can construct that argument.
  - In-repo callers: `bridgePrompts` passes `agentRead`, which has already passed the gate, and `mcp-server-runtime.metadata-outage.test.ts` calls it with three arguments, which takes the unchanged metadata path.
  - `McpMergedMetadataRead` itself did not move in the delta.
- **The new pins are RIGHT and discharge the earlier pins nit.**
  - Case 6 drives a `{ getMetaItems }`-only double. It asserts that the argument names the environment agent `"support_triage"` and not `pkg_helper`, that `getMetaItems` is never called with `{ type: 'agent' }`, and that the environment agent is served. Read against `959a0c61`, this case is red there, because the roster read the protocol listing. That matches the PR body's red-first reading.
  - Case 7: a by-name throw coded `INTERNAL` rejects `prompts/get` with that error, carries no instructions and does not warn `agent prompt refused`. That matches `readAgentByName`'s `throw err` arm and the warn string at the `degraded` branch.
  - Case 8: with the protocol present, a degraded verdict and no names give state `unknown`. The prompt stays listed with no `e.g.`, and the warn carries the verdict's errors. That matches `readAgentRoster` and the `unknown` warn in `bridgePrompts`.
  - The doubles are closures (`vi.fn` over arrow functions), so passing `protocol().getMetaItems` unbound in case 6 is sound. The ablations in the PR body are the dev's own local measurements, and this review did not re-run them.
- **nit (no effect on correctness): `agentReadOf` runs up to three times on one host** (in `bridgePrompts`, in `readAgentRoster` and in `readAgentByName`). It is idempotent, so the decision cannot diverge. The calls inside the two readers are redundant on the `bridgePrompts` path, but they are what gate the exported `buildAgentPromptResult` on its own. Once the gate has passed, `readAgentByName`'s `!read?.getMetaItem` is also redundant.

**Gate verdicts, from the check-runs on this head** (read at 2026-11-08T16:31Z, 50 runs).
- 14 runs concluded `success`: Check Changeset (run 42500113045), Check PR Size, Auto Label, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, both PR-body guards runs, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, Plan Test Core shards, Flag docs affected, Test UI, filter, and Dogfood Regression Gate.
- 15 runs are `skipped`: the UI, docs and opt-in jobs, the schedule gate, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, the Dogfood Regression Gate shards (skipped on `pull_request` by design, #30461), and the duplicate Auto Label and Check PR Size runs from the re-triggered run 42500227245, which started after the 16:30:25Z body edit.
- 21 runs are still `in_progress`, with no conclusion yet: Build Core, all eight Test Core shards, all four Type Check jobs, the ESLint job, the other five Lint jobs, Live E2E UI, and a second Check Changeset (run 42500227245).
- No run has failed. Build, Test Core and Type Check, which carry the unit pins on this head, have not concluded. The dogfood twin did not move, and the merge-queue build measures it, not this head's check-runs.

### ② Semver level

- **`'@objectstack/mcp': patch` is RIGHT.** The delta publishes nothing new. `McpMergedMetadataRead` and `MCPServerRuntime.bridgePrompts`' signature are unchanged since `959a0c61`. `agentReadOf` is module-private, and `buildAgentPromptResult` is not on the package's export map. The net diff still publishes from `@objectstack/mcp` alone. The delta changed only the changeset's prose, and its frontmatter is unchanged. Check Changeset concluded `success` on run 42500113045. Its re-run, 42500227245, is still in progress.
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` HOLDS.** The published widening is unchanged: an optional `getMetaItem` member on the type of `bridgePrompts`' second parameter, and package agents now listed and served on a host whose read has both reads. The delta narrows nothing that `main` publishes. It moves the `{ getMetaItems }`-only host back to `main`'s exact read, so no `(narrowing)` arm is owed. The line is identical in the PR body and the changeset.
